subject: CirrusScale performance follow-up: latency & throughput clarifications
messages:
From: Alex Rinehart <alex@cirrusscale.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.menon@cirrusscale.com>
Date: 2028-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CirrusScale quick demo — perf numbers during call

Hi Soojin / Connor,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — helpful to see the batching and KV-cache behavior. A few quick items from our side as we compare Redwood to our current hyperscaler endpoint: 

- During the call we observed p95 latency differences but want to be precise: can you confirm how Redwood measures p95/p99? Is that per-request excluding client-side retries?
- We have a sustained 64 concurrent connections workload — can Redwood share tokens/sec under a 2k token sequence average with the continuous-batching profile you ran?
- On model parity: we noted you used an LLaMA-variant quantized to 4-bit. Is there a recommendation for a production-safe FP16 vs 4-bit profile for CirrusScale's dataset?

Also attaching our perf logs from the demo to help with alignment. I can loop in security if you need to coordinate account-level VPN for the lab.

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Rinehart
Head of Platform Engineering, CirrusScale
attachments: cirrusscale-demo-logs.tgz
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rinehart <alex@cirrusscale.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-04T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CirrusScale quick demo — perf numbers during call

Alex — great notes, thanks. Quick recap while items are fresh: 

1) Measurement definitions
- p95/p99: Redwood.compute stats at the inference service boundary (token emit time to final token emit) per-request, excluding client retries and routing redirects. We report both server-side "emit" latency and end-to-end (gateway + emit) when relevant.
- For clarity: the numbers we quoted earlier were server emit latencies (gateway overhead ~3–8ms depending on region).

2) Benchmark numbers from today's run (server emit only):
- Continuous batching profile (batching window 10ms, dynamic batching):~
  - Single-client burst (1–4 concurrent): p95 ~ 42ms, p99 ~ 93ms (short prompts, 64 tokens)
  - Sustained 64 concurrent connections, avg payload 2k tokens: tokens/sec (aggregate across pool) ~ 11.5k t/s, median per-request CPU token time ~2.8ms/token
- Quant/Model profiles: FP16 gives slightly higher predictability on p99 vs aggressive 4-bit in long-sequence tails; 4-bit wins on cost and throughput in most steady-state workloads.

3) Suggested A/B test matrix we propose:
- A: Redwood FP16 baseline (autoscale target = 1200 tokens/s per GPU)
- B: Redwood 4-bit quant (autoscale target = 1800 tokens/s per GPU)
- C: CirrusScale hyperscaler managed endpoint (what you had today)
Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 (emit & end-to-end), tokens/sec (aggregate), GPU utilization, and cost per 1M tokens.

4) Next steps we need from CirrusScale:
- Confirm whether you want us to run the A/B runs inside your VPC lab (preferred) or via Redwood-hosted isolated lab. VPC gives more realistic network tails.
- Provide a sample production prompt set (20–30 prompts representative of long-form chat and doc synth) and a target SLA for p95/p99.

I attached: p95-p99-summary.csv (server-emit numbers) and an invite to schedule a 2-day lab window next week (redwood-lab-invite.ics). Connor, Marissa — flagged you for ops and deal alignment.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | redwood.ai
attachments: p95-p99-summary.csv, redwood-lab-invite.ics
From: Alex Rinehart <alex@cirrusscale.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-10-04T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CirrusScale quick demo — perf numbers during call

Thanks Soojin — that helps a lot. Quick clarifications: 

> "server emit" vs "end-to-end"

We will record both, but for procurement we care about end-to-end p99 (user-facing). Can you also provide the gateway overhead distribution (p50/p95/p99) for the US-WEST region from today's run?

> A/B test execution

We prefer Redwood to run the A/B within our VPC — we can provision a test subnet and a bastion host. Security will need to approve inbound/outbound rules. Can you share the minimal IAM and network requirements?

> Scheduling

Targeting Wed/Thu next week (2028-10-11 and 2028-10-12) for the 48-hour run window. If that works we'll lock it. Also — our procurement team has a rolling discount threshold at $X/day based on sustained throughput; we'll want to model costs across the A/B runs so finance can compare.

—Alex
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rinehart <alex@cirrusscale.com>, Priya Menon <priya.menon@cirrusscale.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, security@cirrusscale.com
Date: 2028-10-05T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CirrusScale quick demo — perf numbers during call

Alex / Priya — confirmed next steps and logistics below. Summarizing so procurement & security have a single reference: 

Lab logistics (VPC-hosted A/B runs)
- Redwood needs: one bastion (we will use the ssh key provided), an outbound NAT for image pulls, two t3.small-like test controllers (stateless) and a single dedicated GPU subnet we can reach over the bastion. We'll provide a minimal playbook that lists exact ports (SSH 2200 tunnel, ephemeral worker ports 30000–30100), IAM role with S3-read for model artifacts, and a short-lived service account.
- Security: we will run an initial scanned image and send a SBOM + attestations. Priya, please confirm preferred contact for the SBOM review (security@cirrusscale.com is fine).

Test matrix and measurement plan
- A/B matrix (as above). We'll instrument both server-emit and end-to-end latency. Deliverables after run:
  - p50/p95/p99 server-emit and end-to-end CSVs + raw logs (cirrusscale-benchmark-logs.tar.gz)
  - aggregate tokens/sec and per-GPU throughput report
  - cost projection spreadsheet (cost/1M tokens across config)

Schedule & ownership
- Tentative run dates: 2028-10-11 08:00 PDT -> 2028-10-13 08:00 PDT (48h).
- Ownership: Redwood ops (Connor) will own test execution; Solutions (Soojin) will own analysis; Marissa will drive pricing model to share with procurement.

Action items (who / when)
- CirrusScale: provision test subnet and bastion + send SSH public key by EOD 2028-10-06 (Alex).
- CirrusScale: share prompt set (20–30 prompts) and target SLAs (Priya) by 2028-10-07.
- Redwood: share exact network/IAM playbook and SBOM by 2028-10-06 (Connor).
- Redwood: schedule the 48h run in Calendly and send updated invite (Soojin) once subnet confirmed.

If nobody objects I'll push the Calendly slot tonight and share the RBAC playbook.

Thanks — looking forward.

Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
